candidates.rationale: The source mutates destination memory and requires valid, disjoint source and destination regions. The signature carries no tracked memory permissions through which vstd could express validity, separation, or final contents.
The source performs an overlapping raw-memory copy, but the unit-returning signature exposes neither memory permissions nor a mutable logical state for specifying memmove-style results.
Specifying the delegated nonoverlapping copy requires readable and writable memory-region permissions, disjointness, and final byte contents, none of which are represented by this signature.

The source executes destructor glue through the pointer. A useful contract would require an initialized PointsTo permission and a model of its consumption and destructor effects, but neither is present in the signature.
The source returns Some exactly when the raw pointer is non-null; vstd's raw-pointer view expresses that test as a nonzero data address without inspecting NonNull representation.

Although vstd can express the source's non-null precondition, it has no public NonNull view relating the returned value to ptr. A precondition-only declaration would leave the constructor result unconstrained.
